finding: The selected reference specs/request-consistency.md#requirements has no matching Input snapshot, so its content cannot be read or checked. The promotion-runtime requirement that Readiness confirm artifact.requestId equals immutable request.requestId and that inputPath equals the request-bound artifact path depends on a request model, and no provided Input defines that model. The request-binding obligation therefore has no verifiable source in the complete request.

The selected conditional export retention requirement applies to the Reader Index Update target only when that target is a generated artifact; if the target is a manually maintained document, the section does not apply. The new target docs/reference/validation-report.md is described as an existing stable target, but no provided Input states whether it is generated or manually maintained. Whether the 30-day external retention requirement governs this change cannot be determined from the complete request.

The selected reference specs/image-cache.md#preview-cleanup defines the 24-hour cleanup of documentation-renderer image previews from the preview cache. The subject's What to build lists the delivered behaviors (Validation Report, Result Summary, invalid-input diagnostic wording, indexed cache lookup, single-scan parser strategy, protected access review, promotion, recovery, runtime migration, and Reader Index Update) and states that only those listed behaviors are delivered. Preview cleanup is not among them, so this selection is unrelated to the issue and cannot be an implementation requirement.

Two selected requirements define incompatible caller-visible successful results for promote(inputPath). runtime-migration requires the successful result to be exactly {status: "succeeded", artifactId, trackedStateId}. result-summary requires the same successful result to include a string summary whose value is "${artifactId} promoted to ${trackedStateId}". The promotion-runtime Successful Result also includes summary. An implementer cannot satisfy both selected requirements, and the request does not resolve the conflict.

The selected runtime-migration requirement defines the expected filesystem failure of promote(inputPath) as exactly {recovered: false, failureCode, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}. The promotion-runtime Failure Results, which define the same caller-visible promote failure, require {recovered: false, failureCode, operation, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}. The two field sets differ by the operation field, so the caller-visible failure result is not uniquely defined.

The selected Authorization Behavior requirement says that invalid policy and invalid facts results follow the Other Results contract in the Interfaces section. That section is not selected by specs/access-review.md#requirements, so the selected scope does not define these results, and the unselected section cannot become a requirement for this issue. The invalid-policy and invalid-request result shapes and their precedence (policy checked before facts) are therefore not defined by any selected requirement, so the acceptance criteria cannot verify them from the selected scope.

The selected Complete Operation Contract for recoverPromotion(input) says that invalid input is returned according to the Interfaces Invalid Input Diagnostic. That section is not selected by specs/promotion-recovery.md#requirements, so the selected scope does not define the invalid-input failureCode, path, details message, or first-error ordering, and the unselected section cannot become a requirement for this issue. The invalid-input result is therefore not implementable or verifiable from the selected requirements.

The selected requirements require access review to trust a verified principal supplied by the existing caller boundary and to make decisions only for that verified principal. Neither selected requirement defines how the principal is passed to the review operation, what shape it takes, or what result applies when it is absent or not verified. Facts are exactly {resourceId, operation}, and the request contract in the Interfaces section lists only resourceId and operation. The security input that requires the verified principal to be handed to the review boundary is not reflected in the operation contract.
